top_news.title: Stock Split Watch: Is Eli Lilly (LLY) Stock Next?
top_news.content:
For aficionados of stock splits, it's an intriguing question: Will Eli Lilly (
LLY
+0.88%
) be the next company to split its stock? It certainly might -- its stock price was recently $1,280 per share. But the honest answer is that no one knows (except, perhaps, Lilly's management).

Eli Lilly has split its stock four times -- twice in the 1980s and twice in the 1990s, with the last split happening in October of 1997, nearly 30 years ago. Let's see whether it might do a split again -- and what it means for investors.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Companies generally don't have any pressing need to split their stock, but when shares seem unaffordable for average investors, splitting can make sense. (Not every investor realizes this, but these days, some brokerages permit buying fractions of shares, which can solve the problem of an unaffordable share price.)

Stock splits tend to excite many investors -- because if you own, say, 200 shares of a company, it can feel great to suddenly own, say, 400 shares (via a 2-for-1 split) or 1,000 shares (via a 5-for-1 split). But they're really mostly nothing burgers. Here's why.

Imagine that you own 10 shares of Scruffy's Chicken Shack (ticker: BUKBUK), which is trading at $1,000 per share. The total value of your holding is therefore $10,000. Let's say Scruffy's splits its stock 2-for-1. You'll own 20 shares post-split.

However, share prices are adjusted downward proportionately at the split. So a $1,000 stock becomes a $500 one -- and your 20 shares are now worth ... $10,000 (20 times $500). See? Nothing burger.

Potential stock split aside, should you invest in Eli Lilly? It's worth considering -- because it's doing quite well. Second-quarter revenue was up 48% year over year, largely due to boffo sales for its Mounjaro and Zepbound drugs, which are being used by many to lose weight.

Lilly's stock isn't super cheap right now, though, with a recent price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 41 -- though that's below its five-year average of 58. Still, it might serve long-term investors well.

WisdomTree (NYSE:WT) Shows High Growth Momentum and Breakout Setup
By Mill Chart – Last update: Aug 24, 2026
Quotes Stocks Mentioned
Article Mentions:
WT
(23.51 ▲ 3.80%)

High growth momentum investing starts with a simple premise: the best opportunities often arrive when earnings acceleration and price strength appear at the same time. That is why screening for a high growth momentum rating alongside technical health and setup quality can narrow the field to names that are both fundamentally dynamic and technically actionable. WISDOMTREE INC (NYSE:WT) is one of the stocks that came through that screen with a balanced profile.

What the screen looks for

The high growth momentum rating combines several earnings-related inputs into one score: EPS and sales growth on a year-over-year and sequential basis, acceleration in those metrics, profit margin trends, earnings surprises, and analyst estimate revisions. A score of 6 out of 10 does not signal perfection; it signals that a stock is displaying enough momentum to merit deeper work. The screen then layers on a technical rating of at least 7 and a setup rating of at least 7, with the goal of finding stocks that are not only rising but also consolidating near a potential breakout.

WisdomTree’s growth numbers, on their own, illustrate why the high growth momentum rating sits at 6. The most recent quarter delivered EPS growth of 72.2% over the same period last year, building on a TTM EPS growth rate of 59.4%. Revenue growth followed a similar path, with the last quarter up 57.3% year over year and the TTM figure at 37.1%. Free cash flow per share also jumped 104.9% over the trailing year.

Growth snapshot
High Growth Momentum rating: 6 out of 10
EPS growth (TTM): 59.4%
EPS growth, last quarter vs. year ago: 72.2%
Revenue growth (TTM): 37.1%
Sales growth, last quarter vs. year ago: 57.3%
EPS estimate beats, last 4 quarters: 4 out of 4, average beat 11.2%
Free cash flow growth: 104.9%

One nuance worth noting: revenue estimate revisions have been slightly negative over the past three months, and only two of the last four revenue reports beat estimates. The earnings side is cleaner than the revenue side, but the overall trend remains upward. Analysts still model next-quarter EPS growth of 33.6% and sales growth of 46.6%, which suggests the market sees the momentum continuing. Profit margin also expanded to 25.0% in the latest reported quarter from 11.7% in the prior full year, a sign that the growth is becoming higher quality.

Technical rating and setup quality

On the technical side, WisdomTree leaves little room for criticism. Its ChartMill technical rating is 10 out of 10. The short term and long term trends are both positive, and the stock is trading near a new 52-week high of 23.54. Relative strength is also impressive: WisdomTree has outperformed 93% of all stocks and 98% of the 235 stocks in the Capital Markets industry over the measured period.

The setup quality score is 7 out of 10, which is slightly lower but still constructive. The technical report notes that the stock has been consolidating, volatility has decreased, and there is very little resistance above the current price. Large players have shown interest in recent sessions, which can be a useful confirmation when a breakout is being prepared. The report’s suggested setup places an entry near 23.55, just above the ten-day high, with a stop-loss area at 22.64; the worst-case loss is roughly 3.9%. A detailed look at the support and resistance levels can be found in the technical analysis report.

Why this profile matters

High growth momentum strategies, including those inspired by CANSLIM and Minervini, look for stocks with strong fundamentals and relative strength, but they also require a proper buying point. Buying after a large move can leave little room for error. A consolidation gives the investor a defined entry and a clear level to exit if the trade does not work. WisdomTree offers that combination: the growth metrics support the story, and the chart provides a structure where the risk can be managed.

There are caveats. The setup distance is relatively small, and the technical report notes that the entry and exit levels may be better suited to shorter-term trades. Revenue estimate revisions and revenue beats are less consistent than their earnings counterparts, so the growth story still depends on execution. As with any automatically generated setup, the levels are illustrative and should be checked against upcoming news and earnings events.

Confirmation from other screens

The same investment profile also shows up in related lists, reinforcing the growth and setup story from another angle.

Fastest Growing Stocks: The list highlights WT for "strong recent growth in both earnings and sales," matching the earnings-acceleration part of the thesis.
Breakout Setups: This screen identifies WT as combining "technical strength, constructive consolidation, and enough volatility for a potential breakout," which aligns with the article’s emphasis on an actionable technical setup.

Together, these screens confirm that WisdomTree’s strength is not coming from a single narrow indicator.

Investors looking for additional names that combine high growth momentum with strong technicals and a defined setup can run the same methodology in the stock screener.
